title: Fixed lesson parts, flexible time
statement: Give every lesson the same parts in the same order, and change how much time each part gets rather than whether it appears.
example: In one Grade 9 design, independent practice takes 20% of a first-encounter lesson and 65% of an expert one, while every part still appears.
detail: A Grade 9 lesson design specification says every lesson contains every component, in a fixed order, and that the time each gets changes with the lesson: components are modules of variable length, not fixed slides, and its profiles move independent practice from 20% of a first-encounter lesson to 65% of an expert one (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, lines 29, 196, 218, 222 and 293). A Grade 3 reading course's lesson design likewise fixes the lesson's shape and lets only its block of tasks flex (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, line 115). Neither design reports an outcome.
against: Neither shape is rigid: the Grade 3 design lets whole parts give way when a child is slow, its Magic Doors first (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, lines 352 and 358), and in the Grade 9 specification only unit-opening lessons begin with the unit video and review lessons change the form of guided practice (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, lines 29 and 224).
